title: Week 10 MFPI analysis: Tupelo High School leads the statewide rankings
dek: What moved in the Week 10 Mississippi Football Power Index, computed from verified results through Nov 3.
author: MFPI automated analysis

sources.label: MHSAA official score center (schedules and scores)
Statewide media rankings used for the Media Rank inputs

limitations: Generated from the published snapshot; no games after the cutoff are included.
Media Rank and Media Strength of Schedule contribute 20% of every rating; MFPI's own score-based model contributes 80%.
No player, injury, coaching or game-narrative information is used or implied.

sections.heading: The top of the statewide rankings
paragraphs: [[tupelo]] (10-0) is No. 1 for the 10th straight published week. MFPI rating: decreased 0.4 points to 96.8. In the latest window it beat [[lewisburg]] (currently No. 83) 44-0 on the road on Oct 29.
No. 2 [[gulfport]] (8-1, 7A): ranking unchanged at No. 2; rating increased 1.2 points to 96.3. It beat [[diberville]] (currently No. 3) 28-24 at home on Oct 30.
No. 3 [[diberville]] (8-1, 7A): ranking up 1 spot to No. 3 (from No. 4); rating increased 0.7 points to 93.9. It lost to [[gulfport]] (currently No. 2) 24-28 on the road on Oct 30.
No. 4 [[warren-central]] (9-0, 6A): ranking down 1 spot to No. 4 (from No. 3); rating decreased 0.9 points to 93.4. It beat [[callaway]] (currently No. 103) 49-0 at home on Oct 30.
No. 5 [[brandon]] (7-2, 7A): ranking up 3 spots to No. 5 (from No. 8); rating increased 1.1 points to 92.6. It beat [[pearl]] (currently No. 59) 43-8 at home on Oct 30.

sections.heading: Classification leaders
paragraphs: Class ranks are the statewide order filtered to one classification; MFPI never recalculates a separate class rating.
Every classification kept the same No. 1 team as the previous week.

sections.heading: Results that raised ratings most
paragraphs: The largest rating increases among teams with a verified result in this window. A rating can also move without a game, because every opponent's rating is re-solved each week.
[[holmes-county-central]] (+5.5 to 45.7, now No. 126) beat [[vicksburg]] (currently No. 98) 26-14 on the road on Oct 30.
[[horn-lake]] (+5.0 to 67.4, now No. 66) beat [[southaven]] (currently No. 76) 26-0 on the road on Oct 30.
[[biloxi]] (+4.8 to 69.7, now No. 56) beat [[west-harrison]] (currently No. 63) 38-22 on the road on Oct 30.
[[lanier]] (+4.8 to 64.7, now No. 71) beat [[cleveland-central]] (currently No. 51) 26-18 at home on Oct 30.
[[nettleton]] (+4.8 to 26.4, now No. 180) lost to [[winona]] (currently No. 34) 22-50 on the road on Oct 29.
The full list of movers is in the [[risers-and-fallers:2026-week-10-risers-and-fallers]] analysis.

sections.heading: Schedule strength
paragraphs: MFPI strength of schedule is the average current rating of every completed opponent, expressed as a statewide percentile (100 is the strongest schedule in this week's field, not a perfect grade). The five strongest schedules: [[germantown]] (5-5, SOS percentile 100.0); [[northwest-rankin]] (3-6, SOS percentile 99.6); [[west-point]] (2-7, SOS percentile 99.1); [[madison-central]] (5-4, SOS percentile 98.7); [[brandon]] (7-2, SOS percentile 98.2).

Teams that have played furthest above their own classification (average class steps up, games up in class): [[okolona]] (1A, +1.38, 5 up); [[charleston]] (2A, +1.20, 5 up); [[byers]] (1A, +1.14, 4 up); [[poplarville]] (4A, +1.11, 5 up); [[biggersville]] (1A, +1.11, 6 up).

sections.heading: Data notes and limitations
paragraphs: Snapshot generated November 3, 2026 at 11:11 AM Central with a cutoff of November 3 at 11:00 AM Central, formula MFPI-3.2.
1087 of 1110 game listings due by the cutoff had verified scores (97.9%); the rest count as unavailable, never as losses or 0-0 results.
[[wesson]] is credited with two games on Oct 23. One listing may belong to a same-named school; it is under review and affects that team and its opponents.
Opponent ranks in this article are the opponent's rank in this snapshot, not its rank on the day the game was played, unless a sentence says otherwise.
